name: What is one's own / the faculty of judgment
originalThought: QUELLE: The clear 'dichotomy of control' is primarily Epictetus, Enchiridion 1 — NOT Marcus. Marcus expresses related ideas: 12.22 'everything is opinion, and opinion is in thy power'; 6.8 (the ruling faculty); 5.19 (things do not touch the soul). Attribution to Marcus is deliberately LOW.
softwareInterpretation: INTERPRETATION: Code should clearly separate its controllable state from uncontrollable external influences (I/O, time, randomness, global state); side effects should be visible and bounded.
preconditions: A unit whose name/signature suggests purity, so hidden side effects are detectable as a discrepancy.
limits: 'Expected purity' is estimated from name/signature -> false-positive risk; language idioms differ. Low attribution to Marcus remains visible in the finding (see Epictetus as primary source).
counterexamples: A clearly named main()/Repository/Service method whose purpose is I/O.
Deliberately encapsulated state inside a class.

changelog.note: Initial version (MVP). Flagged low attribution; Epictetus is the primary source and a candidate second knowledge-base source.
